The yellow line is the gray line. The red dot is your QTH.

The gray line (terminator) is the band along the boundary between day and night. The ionosphere behaves in a special way there – the D layer (which absorbs lower frequencies) fades before nightfall, while the F layers stay ionised enough to reflect radio waves.\n\nThanks to this, stations lying on the same gray line can make unusually long DX contacts (gray-line propagation) on 160 m, 80 m or 40 m with minimal signal loss.
